title: Teaching Strategies and Approaches for Pupils with Special Educational Needs: A Scoping Study
venue: Research Report RR516, Department for Education and Skills (DfES)
extended_summary:
This report asks what teaching strategies and approaches are most effective for pupils with special educational needs (SEN), what theoretical perspectives support those approaches, and how best-practice knowledge might be used in everyday teaching. It was commissioned as a four-month scoping study and explicitly aimed to map existing evidence across the full range of SEN rather than to test a single intervention. The authors organised the literature using the SEN Code of Practice areas of need: communication and interaction, cognition and learning, behavioural/emotional/social development, and sensory and/or physical needs.

The report synthesises national and international reviews, research reports, and professional guidance, drawing on evidence from schools and other educational settings across the full age range of compulsory education and early years. It does not present a single empirical sample; instead, it reviews patterns in the literature for groups such as children with speech, language and communication needs, autistic spectrum disorder, learning difficulties, behavioural difficulties, and sensory/physical disabilities. The review notes that much of the evidence is practitioner-oriented or based on small studies, with substantial variation in methods and outcomes.

The main conclusion is that while certain approaches appear promising—such as early intervention, parent collaboration, visual supports, intensive interaction, explicit literacy teaching, metacognitive supports, peer-mediated strategies, self-regulation approaches, environmental adaptations, and the use of technology—these strategies are not sufficiently distinct from general good teaching to justify a separate SEN pedagogy. The report argues instead for inclusive pedagogy informed by special education knowledge, and it recommends longer-term development work in real school settings to test combinations of strategies and their effects on achievement.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a scoping review/grey report rather than a primary empirical study, meta-analysis, or controlled evaluation. It synthesizes prior literature narratively and does not present a rigorous study design or new quantitative effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The report has practical relevance for SEN pedagogy and policy, but it does not demonstrate a measurable intervention effect in this paper. Its impact is therefore indirect and uncertain, based on literature synthesis rather than observed outcomes.
